question: Does God dwell in temples?
summary: 1 Kings 8:13 and 2 Chronicles 7:12, 16 declare that God's name and presence will dwell in the Jerusalem temple Solomon built. Acts 7:48 (Stephen's speech) and Acts 17:24 (Paul at the Areopagus) flatly deny that the Most High dwells in temples made with hands. The same deity is depicted as both occupying a specific building and refusing to occupy any building.

reconcile.connective: Commentators read the two as compatible: God's name and glory rested in Solomon's temple, yet the Most High was never confined or contained by any building.

discrepancy.connective: Marcel Simon argues the case is genuinely disputed, reading Stephen's "made with hands" speech as a real anti-Temple theology at odds with the Kings and Chronicles claim that God chose the temple to dwell in.

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: Such an one as Solomon's was; he did indeed dwell in his temple, but he was not confined to it, nor included in it, or circumscribed by it; and so much Solomon himself suggests, when he expresses his wonder at his dwelling on earth, seeing the heaven of heavens could not contain him, and still less the house which he had built, Kg1 8:27 …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly harmonizes both sides: God truly dwelt in Solomon's temple yet was not confined to it, citing Solomon's own words (1 Kings 8:27) that the heavens cannot contain him.
